did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ecclesiastes uses a striking image: even dead flies can ruin a perfumer’s expensive oil. In the same way, a little foolishness can spoil wisdom and honor.

Did you know? Ecclesiastes describes the wise person’s heart as inclined to the right and the fool’s heart as inclined to the left. Even as he goes along the road, the fool reveals his lack of understanding and makes it known to everyone.
Did you know? When a ruler’s anger rises against you, Ecclesiastes advises you not to leave your place. According to the verse, patience and calmness can quiet and moderate serious offenses or anger.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes calls a ruler’s mistake “an evil under the sun,” because such an error can distort the social and political order.

Did you know? To illustrate the reversal of the proper order, Ecclesiastes describes servants riding on horses while princes walk on the ground. It portrays a situation in which social classes are not functioning as they should.

Did you know? The chapter contains several warnings about actions that can turn against the person who carries them out: the one who digs a pit may fall into it, and the one who breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

Did you know? Ecclesiastes notes that a blunt iron tool requires more effort and concludes that sharpening the tool gives an advantage. This illustrates the importance of preparation, skill, and wisdom before taking action.

Did you know? The verse about the snake emphasizes that the charmer’s usefulness depends on timing: if the snake has already bitten and no charm came before the bite, there is no advantage for the one who is supposed to control it with his words.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes contrasts the words of the wise, which are gracious, with the lips of the fool, which can swallow up and harm him.

Did you know? Ecclesiastes warns against cursing a king or a rich person even in the privacy of your bedroom or in your thoughts, because what is said or thought in secret may be revealed and reach the powerful person.
